column1: # Case table for substrate/.github/workflows/caixa-auto-release.yml
# TAB-separated: <name> <context k=v;k=v> <expect-run csv> <expect-skip csv>
# WHAT THIS PINS. Two jobs, and exactly two facts decide which of them run:
#   bump  if: github.actor != 'github-actions[bot]'      (no needs)
#   ship  if: needs.bump.outputs.bumped == 'true'        (needs: bump)
# So the table's job is to hold three claims still: a bump publishes, a no-bump
# does not, and the bot's own push does not re-enter the loop.
# WHY IT EXISTS. On 2026-08-08 pleme-io/graphql-synthesizer ran the sibling
# cargo-auto-release, reported SUCCESS, bumped + tagged + pushed, and published
# nothing — its ship job carried `&& !github.event.repository.private` and was
# silently skipped. A deliberate no-publish and a broken no-publish were the
# same green tick, because nobody had written down which jobs must run.
# READ ROW 2 BEFORE CHANGING ANYTHING. caixa-auto-release does NOT carry that
# privacy guard in any `if:`, and that is deliberate, not an oversight. It reads
# github.event.repository.private twice, but only inside `runs-on`, where it
# picks a self-hosted label so a private consumer is not billed for metered
# minutes — a runner selector, never a selection gate. The reason the guard is
# absent here and present in cargo-auto-release is the DESTINATION of the
# publish: caixa-publish pushes a rendered Helm chart to our own OCI registry,
# where a private repo shipping a private artifact is the correct outcome;
# cargo publish pushes to the public crates.io index, where it would leak the
# source and where a yank cannot be undone. Same shape, opposite right answer.
# `github.event.repository.private` is therefore declared in every case even
# though no `if:` reads it. It is the axis the sibling workflow turns on, and a
# row that did not state it would leave the next reader unable to tell whether
# this workflow was checked against it or merely never thought about. If a
# `&& !github.event.repository.private` is ever added to ship, row 2 goes red
# and the change has to be argued for rather than absorbed.
# 1. The happy path on a public repo: a bump publishes.
public-bump-publishes
# 2. THE ROW THAT WAS MISSING WHEN graphql-synthesizer SHIPPED NOTHING — asserted
#    here with the OPPOSITE expectation, on purpose. A private caixa repo DOES
#    publish, because the artifact goes to our own OCI registry and never to a
#    public index. See the header. Do not "fix" this row to match the cargo one.
private-bump-publishes
# 3. Nothing to release: bump runs and finds no change, so ship must not fire.
#    This is the case that keeps ship's condition from being weakened to always().
public-no-bump
# 4. The bot's own commit-and-push must not re-trigger the pipeline. bump is
#    skipped by the actor guard; ship is skipped both by its own condition and by
#    needs-propagation. The empty value models a SKIPPED upstream job, which is a
#    distinct state from 'false' — bump never ran, so it emitted no output at all.
bot-actor-no-loop
